pointer - verticator filters: - code-fullscreen - reveal-auto-agenda editor: source order: 3 --- ## Learning Outcomes - Introduction to Statistical Learning - Classification vs Regression - Supervised vs Unsupervised Machine Learning ## Python Modules, Functions, and Parameters ::: {#b888fff7 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import pandas as pd from plotnine import * from pygam import LinearGAM, s, l import statsmodels.api as sm from statsmodels.gam.api import GLMGam, BSplines from sklearn.datasets import load_iris from sklearn.neighbors import KNeighborsClassifier from sklearn.metrics import confusion_matrix from sklearn.svm import SVC rng = np.random.default_rng(909) ``` ::: ## Book ![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/5ff2adbe3fe4fe33db902812/1611294680091-25SIDM9AHA8ECIFFST23/Screen+Shot+2021-01-21+at+11.02.06+AM.png){fig-align="center"} # Introduction to Statistical Learning ## Introduction to Statistical Learning **What is Statistical Learning?** ::: {#.fragment} Statistical learning is the task of predicting an outcome of interest given a set of predictor variables. ::: ## Motivating Example ::: {#7dab8009 .cell execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-3-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## Statistical Learning Model $$ Y = f(\boldsymbol X) + \varepsilon $$ - $Y$: Outcome variable - $f(\cdot)$: systematic component explaining $Y$ - $\boldsymbol X$: vector of predictor variables - $\varepsilon$: error term ## Modeling $f(\cdot)$: Parametric - Linear Models - Generalized Linear Models (GLM) ## Modeling $f(\cdot)$: Nonparametric - Generalized Additive Models - Local-Linear Models - Smoothing Splines ## Prediction - Statistical Learning is only concerned with an accurate $Y$ - $f(\cdot)$ is considered a black box - We will not know how $\boldsymbol X$ explains $Y$ - We choose flexible (nonparametric) models ## Model Interpretability - With a focus on prediction, model interpretability declines - We will not know how changes in $\boldsymbol X$ will affect $Y$ # Classification vs Regression ## Regression Regression in statistical learning terms indicates predicting a continuous random variable.
What are the methods that we learned to model continuous random variables?

## Example ::: panel-tabset ## Data ::: {#28cc3535 .cell execution_count=8} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=8} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-9-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## KNN ::: {#456f3105 .cell execution_count=9} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Predicted setosa versicolor virginica Actual setosa 20 0 0 versicolor 0 18 2 virginica 0 2 18 ``` ::: ::: ## SVM ::: {#0db8ea46 .cell execution_count=10} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Actual setosa versicolor virginica Predicted setosa 50 0 0 versicolor 0 48 2 virginica 0 2 48 ``` ::: ::: ::: # Supervised vs Unsupervised Machine Learning ## Machine Learning Machine learning is a set of methods used for predicting and classifying data. Several statistical methods are considered machine learning techniques. ::: {#.fragement} #### Common Methods - Regression - Mixed-Effects - Nonparametric Regression - Neural Networks - Tree-based methods - Bayesian Methods ::: ## Training Data Training Data is the data set used to construct a model. ## Supervised Supervised Machine Learning techniques are techniques where the training data contains the outcome. ## Unsupervised Unsupervised Machine Learning techniques are techniques where the training data **does not** contains the outcome. # Model Adequacy ## Quality of Fit: Regression $$ MSE = \frac{1}{n}\sum^n_{i=1}\{y_i - \hat f(\boldsymbol x_i)\}^2 $$ ## Quality of Fit: Classification $$ ER = \frac{1}{n}\sum^n_{i=1}I(y_i \ne \hat y_i) $$ ## Bias-Variance Tradeoff ## Bias-Variance Tradeoff $$ E(MSE) = E\left\{y-\hat f(x)\right\}^2 = Var\left\{\hat f(x)\right\} + Bias\left\{\hat f(x)\right\}^2 $$ ## Example ::: {#b68bdee9 .cell execution_count=11} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=11} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-12-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## Using a Line ::: {#0bd19596 .cell execution_count=12} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=12} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-13-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## Using a Highly Flexible Model ::: {#80911472 .cell execution_count=13} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=13} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-14-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## Semi-Flexible ::: {#153aadbf .cell execution_count=14} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=14} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-15-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: ::: ## All ::: {#e1638db3 .cell execution_count=15} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=15} ![](2a_files/figure-revealjs/cell-16-output-1.png){width=960 height=480} ::: :::
